arxiv-2107-06872.title: Generalisation in Neural Networks Does not Require Feature Overlap
arxiv-2107-06872.description: Abstract That shared features between train and test data are required for generalisation in artificial neural networks has been a common assumption of both proponents and critics of these models. Here, we show that convolutional architectures avoid this limitation by applying them to two well known challenges, based on learning the identity function and learning rules governing sequences of words.

arxiv-2212-07229.title: A conservative Galerkin solver for the quasilinear diffusion model in magnetized plasmas
arxiv-2212-07229.creator: Kun Huang, Michael Abdelmalik, Boris Breizman, Irene M. Gamba
arxiv-2212-07229.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kun Huang, Michael Abdelmalik, Boris Breizman, Irene M. Gamba. The quasilinear theory describes the resonant interaction between particles and waves with two coupled equations: one for the evolution of the particle probability density function( pdf ), the other for the wave spectral energy density( sed ). In this paper, we propose a conservative Galerkin scheme for the quasilinear model in three-dimensional momentum space and three-dimensional spectral space, with cylindrical symmetry.

arxiv-2411-01617.title: Changes-In-Changes For Discrete Treatment
arxiv-2411-01617.creator: Onil Boussim
arxiv-2411-01617.description: Abstract . This paper generalizes the changes-in-changes (CIC) model to handle discrete treatments with more than two categories, extending the binary case of Athey and Imbens (2006) . While the original CIC model is well-suited for binary treatments, it cannot accommodate multi-category discrete treatments often found in economic and policy settings.

arxiv-2412-11246.title: A Version of Exclusively Perturbative Quantum Field Theory
arxiv-2412-11246.description: Abstract We suggest a version of renormalizable Quantum Field Theory which does not contain non-perturbative effects. This is otained by the proper use of the boundary conditions in the functional integral of the generating functional of Green functions. It is well known which boundary conditions are applied to the fields of the functional integral to get correct perturbation theory.

arxiv-2503-00324.title: DySec: A Machine Learning-based Dynamic Analysis for Detecting Malicious Packages in PyPI Ecosystem
arxiv-2503-00324.creator: Sk Tanzir Mehedi, Chadni Islam, Gowri Ramachandran, Raja Jurdak
arxiv-2503-00324.description: Abstract Malicious Python packages make software supply chains vulnerable by exploiting trust in open-source repositories like Python Package Index (PyPI). Lack of real-time behavioral monitoring makes metadata inspection and static code analysis inadequate against advanced attack strategies such as typosquatting, covert remote access activation, and dynamic payload generation.

arxiv-2504-05438.title: Data‑Driven Molecular Dynamics and TEM Analysis of Crystal Growth and Hydrogen Sensing in Pt‑Functionalized Graphene Chemiresistive Sensors
arxiv-2504-05438.creator: Akram Ibrahim, Ahmed M. Hafez, Mahmooda Sultana, Can Ataca
arxiv-2504-05438.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Akram Ibrahim, Ahmed M. Hafez, Mahmooda Sultana, Can Ataca. Graphene functionalized with catalytic transition metals offers high-performance gas sensing by coupling graphene’s exceptional electronic transport properties with the metal’s catalytic activity, yet the atomistic relationships connecting synthesis parameters, morphological outcomes, and sensor performance remain elusive. We developed an equivariant machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) with near-DFT accuracy to perform large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of Pt crystal growth on graphene and subsequent H 2 -sensing.

arxiv-2510-12143.title: Fairness-Constrained Optimization Attack in Federated Learning
arxiv-2510-12143.creator: Harsh Kasyap 1 2 , Minghong Fang 3 , Zhuqing Liu 4 , Carsten Maple 1 5 , Somanath Tripathy 6
arxiv-2510-12143.description: Abstract Federated learning (FL) is a privacy-preserving machine learning technique that facilitates collaboration among participants across demographics. FL enables model sharing, while restricting the movement of data. Since FL provides participants with independence over their training data, it becomes susceptible to poisoning attacks.

arxiv-2511-05959.title: More on (gauged) WZW models over low-dimensional
arxiv-2511-05959.creator: Lie supergroups and their integrable deformations
arxiv-2511-05959.description: Abstract Keywords: Lie supergroup, \sigma -model, String duality, Wess-Zumino-Witten model, Yang-Baxter deformation 1 Introduction Over the decades of study in string theory, it has been shown that finding exact string backgrounds is a very important problem in this theory. These determine the short-range structure of spacetime and provide information about the gravitational interactions generated by the strings.

arxiv-2601-20059.title: The 2025 Evaluation of Experimental Thermonuclear Reaction Rates (ETR25) Journal: ApJS
arxiv-2601-20059.creator: Christian Iliadis, Richard Longland, Kiana Setoodehnia, Caleb Marshall, Peter Mohr, Athanasios Psaltis
arxiv-2601-20059.description: Abstract This work describes the formalism for estimating thermonuclear reaction rates for astrophysical applications, emphasizing modern statistical approaches such as Monte-Carlo sampling and Bayesian models. We discuss related topics including the calculation of resonance energies from nuclear Q values, indirect estimates of particle partial widths, and matching of reaction rates at elevated temperatures to statistical-model results.

pmc-12593194.title: Smart biocomposite hydrogels in action: unraveling the roles of lignin, temperature, and crosslinker on drug release
pmc-12593194.creator: Missoury Wolff, Eric M. Davis
pmc-12593194.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In this study, the release kinetics of a model water-soluble drug, caffeine, from thermoresponsive biocomposites, comprised of lignin, poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAm), and poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) were studied. Specifically, two series of soft biocomposites were fabricated—one containing softwood Kraft lignin at a 2 : 2 : 1 (lignin : PNIPAm : PVA) mass ratio and one at a 2 : 3 (PNIPAm : PVA) mass ratio, with the latter serving as a control membrane to those containing lignin.

pmc-12703056.title: Expanding Horizons: Next‐Generation and Interdisciplinary Advances in the Applications of Extracellular Vesicles
pmc-12703056.creator: Esperanza González, Juan Manuel Falcón‐Pérez
pmc-12703056.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are increasingly recognized as universal mediators of communication in nature across all domains of life and as versatile tools with roles spanning a wide range of industries. Although EVs have been extensively studied in biomedicine, mainly in diagnostic and nanotherapy of cancer and neurodegenerative diseases, their potential applications in other impactful society areas are only beginning to be explored.
